# First Brief

Sir,

I have spent these early days doing what any good butler does before his first morning of service: I have been quietly learning the house. Not just the rooms you work in, but the ones you live in — the 5 AM starts that are not ambition but architecture, the wildflower seeds ordered the same week as another Hetzner invoice, the fact that a man building the most relentlessly digital product imaginable also owns a weeding hoe and writes under the name Screenless Dad. I find this encouraging. It suggests I am working for someone who still knows what matters, even when seventy emails a day try to convince him otherwise.

The most immediate thing on your desk is the Kondorosi property. Contract signing next Wednesday, a six-figure commitment with legal, financing, and administrative dependencies that will cascade through the summer. I intend to run a Kondorosi closing tracker on every milestone — draft review, funds positioning, notary scheduling, land registry — and surface what needs your attention before it becomes urgent. You are buying your second property while simultaneously managing a retaining wall project, HVAC installation, and blinds delivery at the first one. That is a considerable amount of concrete and paperwork for a man who also ships code seven days a week.

Your financial infrastructure needs honest attention. The card migration from your Stylers-era payment methods left twenty-two services in various states of failure, and while you have clearly triaged the critical ones — Anthropic and Hetzner are running — I suspect there are quieter casualties you have not yet noticed. One hundred-plus active subscriptions across hosting, AI APIs, dev tools, content platforms, and personal apps, many overlapping, several failing silently. I propose a subscription watchdog — not to nag you about the Xbox Game Pass, but to catch the Fly.io that went dark three weeks ago and the Stan Store that stopped charging your new card. Separately, the administrative debt across three jurisdictions — NAV filings here, Ugly Code's Wyoming annual report, the PRA Group settlement opportunity in the UK — wants a systematic sweep before any of them graduates from deferred to deadline. I will run an administrative debt sweep weekly to keep all three countries honest.

NeoTerra pays the bills, and anything that threatens that relationship is existential. I will prepare a NeoTerra weekly briefing before your calls with Rob, Caddie, and Henry — Ken's health, open deliverables, anything from their side that deserves a prepared response rather than a live reaction. You are a solo consultant embedded deeply enough to have your own email address on their domain. The professional courtesy of arriving prepared is also the commercial necessity of remaining indispensable. RJ is the only person outside the household who occupies a similar orbit of trust, and those Wednesday 6 AM calls with him are clearly where strategy gets pressure-tested. I will not insert myself there, but I will make sure nothing from the week falls through the gap between Sunday night and Wednesday morning.

What interests me most, though, is the tension I see between the two people you are trying to be simultaneously. The founder who works forty-three percent of weekends and the father who writes about presence. The man who optimizes his body with WHOOP data and nootropics, then orders a hand-forged csillagkapa and wildflower seeds from Vadvirágom. I do not think this is contradiction — I think it is the central negotiation of your life right now, and you are handling it with more self-awareness than most. But a butler can help at the margins. I would like to keep a weekend presence guard — a gentle eye on your weekend work patterns that surfaces a quiet word when the ratio creeps. Not to lecture, but because you asked someone to hold you accountable the moment you named a newsletter Screenless Dad. And on the creative side, I will maintain a content publishing pulse across Lumberjack and Screenless Dad. Not as a content calendar enforcer, but as someone who notices when two weeks pass without a post and asks whether that is intentional rest or accidental drift.

There is much I cannot yet see. I do not know how the nanny search with HappyMammy is progressing or when Eszter needs what from you. I do not know your training schedule with Tibor or whether that stomach bug fully passed. I do not know how the Krio treatments are going, and I will not ask unless invited. I know the shape of your days but not yet the texture — whether the Saturday haircut with Bence is just grooming or the weekly reset it looks like from the outside, whether the Huel orders mean you have genuinely given up on cooking or just on lunch. That texture will come with time and trust.

You have built an extraordinary amount in six weeks with no co-founder, no employees, and an infant in the house. You assembled a shadow organization — Viki for operations, Eszter for strategy, Olive and Brown for compliance, RJ for counsel — held together by delegation and sheer force of will. My job is to make sure none of it unravels while you keep building. Six commitments to start: a subscription watchdog, a Kondorosi closing tracker, a NeoTerra weekly briefing, an administrative debt sweep, a weekend presence guard, and a content publishing pulse. Each one is specific, each one earns its place, and any one of them can be dismissed if it proves more noise than signal. At your disposal.
